_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: Prana
suggestions.reason: Two floors of proper acoustics on Ashley Road from the team behind Stockport's Amp — order the cocktail, but the stage is the reason to stay past nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), whatpub.com and Altrincham Today: Prana, 14-16 Ashley Road, Altrincham WA14 2DW, an independent live-music venue and cocktail bar opened November 2023, run by the same team as Amp in Stockport — a real 2-site sibling pair, not a chain, same precedent as Bramhall/Cheadle Hulme's Mounting Stone/Chiverton Tap pair in this batch. RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-11 (curia-suggestion-review) found the original researcher's 'CAMRA-listed and actively promoted' claim was incomplete: CAMRA and whatpub.com both actually list Prana as 'Closed Long Term' (last updated 28/05/2024), following a reported 'closing until further notice' Facebook announcement from Altrincham Today around the same date — a real closure signal the original pass missed. However, a new company, PRANA F&B LIMITED, was incorporated 13 September 2024 at the same 14-16 Ashley Road address and remains active per Companies House, and a Food Hygiene Ratings record exists for 'Prana - Altrincham' — both consistent with a reopening or change of hands rather than the site sitting empty, but no direct evidence of current 2025/2026 trading (a recent event listing, an active social post) was found either way. Genuinely conflicting signals rather than a clean pass or fail — left pending here and sent to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than promoted or rejected outright.

suggestions.name: Picturedrome
suggestions.reason: The third room from the Mackie Mayor and Altrincham Market team, built into the shell of Macclesfield's oldest cinema — sourdough pizza and rare-breed steak sandwiches under a ceiling that's been feeding a crowd since 1911.
suggestions.researchNotes: Macclesfield had zero seeded venues at all before this run (added as a district 2026-09-11, no venues yet — the most acute coverage gap found today, ahead of every other under-10 district). Verified via confidentials.com, creativetourist.com and visitmacclesfield.co.uk: Picturedrome, 102-104 Chestergate, Macclesfield SK11 6DU, opened 2019 in a 1911 cinema building. Explicitly the 'spiritual sister' of Mackie Mayor (Northern Quarter) and Altrincham Market, both already in venues.json — same operators (Nick Johnson, Jenny Thompson and team), same MARKET HALL type reused, a real 3-site small-group precedent no different from the 2-3-site sibling pairs already accepted throughout this file (Cibo/Suburban Green, Wallop, etc.). Coordinates from the postcode centroid (SK11 6DU), which lands on Chestergate as expected. High confidence: well-documented, actively trading, no closure signals found.

suggestions.name: Chestergate Bistro
suggestions.reason: Sixteen years on Chestergate under two owners and one register — Aberdeen Angus fillet and confit duck done properly, at prices that haven't chased the postcode's newer arrivals.
suggestions.researchNotes: Second of today's Macclesfield candidates, closing the district's Eat gap. Verified via the operator's own site (chestergatebistro.co.uk), visitmacclesfield.co.uk and Companies House (CHESTERGATE BISTRO LTD): 66 Chestergate, Macclesfield SK11 6DY, open since 2009, independent and family-run, now under its second owner but never operated as a group or chain — single site only, no other locations found anywhere. Introduces a new type, BISTRO — no existing type fits a modern-British-with-French-influence bistro precisely (FRENCH BISTRO, used for Cure Bistro in Heaton Moor, implies a specifically French kitchen, which this isn't); left category-only (Eat) in the same manner as CANTONESE ROAST/GREEK TAVERNA elsewhere in this file. Also a plausible fit for the 'Neighbourhood favourite' Eat tile given its 16-year single-site run, though not mapped there directly (that tile currently keys off specific cuisine types, not a BISTRO type — a call for tile-catalog-map.ts, not this entry). High confidence: independently and consistently reviewed (4.7/5 on Tripadvisor, #6 of 167 Macclesfield restaurants), no closure signals.

suggestions.name: MASH
suggestions.reason: The only room in Macclesfield still running a Wednesday-to-Friday live set off a sixties-and-seventies-themed stage, then handing Saturday to a vinyl night that skips anything too recent.
suggestions.researchNotes: Third and final Macclesfield candidate today, giving the district its first Drink-category venue alongside Picturedrome (Do) and Chestergate Bistro (Eat) — a deliberate one-per-category spread for a district that had zero venues this morning. Verified via whatpub.com, Macclesfield Nub News and the venue's own listings: MASH, 5 Back Wallgate, Macclesfield SK11 6LQ, part of the town's Castle Quarter, an independent 60s/70s-themed bar and small live-music venue with live sets Wed-Fri, a Saturday vinyl night and Sunday open-mic. No chain footprint or sibling sites found anywhere. Type reused from Butchers Bar (Hale)'s existing LIVE MUSIC BAR. Moderate-high confidence: consistently reviewed across whatpub/Tripadvisor/Facebook with recent activity, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Amici
suggestions.reason: Andrea, Giovanni and Chris's own room just inside the precinct, Italian plates turning Greek by the second course — small, bustling, and exactly what a village square this size is supposed to produce.
suggestions.researchNotes: Bramhall stood at 3 venues (1 Do, 1 Drink, 1 Eat) before this run — one of the under-10 districts from the standing priority. Verified via Companies House (AMICI (BRAMHALL) LIMITED, a standalone entity, not a subsidiary of a chain), bramhallvillagesquare.co.uk and Tripadvisor: Amici, 14-15 The Bramhall Centre, Bramhall, Stockport SK7 1AW, a recently opened Italian-Greek restaurant and bar, co-owned by Andrea, Giovanni and Chris. Co-owner Giovanni's background is at Piccolino (a large national Italian chain, itself never a candidate here) — flagged and checked specifically because of that association, but Amici itself has exactly one site, its own separate limited company, and no evidence of any second location or expansion plan; a personal chef/restaurateur background at a chain does not make their new independent venture one. High confidence: real, recently opened, well-reviewed, single-site.

suggestions.name: Long Bar & Kitchen
suggestions.reason: Espresso martinis and a globally-leaning small-plates menu on Ack Lane East — booth seating built for a table that has no intention of leaving after the first round.
suggestions.researchNotes: Second Bramhall candidate today, giving the district a second Drink venue alongside The Mounting Stone (already seeded) and rounding it toward 5 total. Verified via Food Hygiene Ratings, bramhallvillagesquare.co.uk and Tripadvisor: Long Bar & Kitchen, 8 Ack Lane East, Bramhall, Stockport SK7 2BY, an independent bar and small-plates kitchen (global/Asian-leaning menu, strong cocktail list). No parent company, sibling site or chain footprint found anywhere despite a specific search for one — single site as far as independently verifiable. Moderate-high confidence: well-reviewed (4.4/5, #14 of 30 Bramhall restaurants), active and current, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Avanti Restaurant & Grill
suggestions.reason: Chico's own dining room on Moorside Road since 2006 — proper Italian plates and the kind of welcome that means regulars stop reading the menu.
suggestions.researchNotes: Heaton Moor stood at 3 venues (1 Do, 1 Drink, 1 Eat) before this run — another under-10 district from the standing priority. Verified via Companies House (AVANTI RESTAURANT & GRILL LTD), the operator's own site (dineatavanti.co.uk) and Food Hygiene Ratings: 1 Moorside Road, Heaton Moor, Stockport SK4 4DT, privately owned since 2006, single site, no chain or sibling-site footprint found anywhere. High confidence: long-established, consistently reviewed, no closure signals. Note: while researching Heaton Moor's food/drink scene, Damson and La Cantina (a converted half of the same building) were both investigated and explicitly rejected — their owner Steve Pilling runs a real 9-10-site restaurant/bar group across Manchester (Damson MediaCity, two Dockyards, Vesper, Lost in Tokyo, Moortop, Produce Hall and others), well past this file's small-sibling-group allowance; Eden (54 Heaton Moor Road) was also researched and dropped on a genuinely unclear-ownership signal (conflicting reports of a Vinehop-of-Poynton takeover that may not have completed) rather than guessed at.

suggestions.name: Heaton Moor Producers Market
suggestions.reason: First Sunday of the month, Shaw Road car park, independent stallholders only — the kind of market that never quite showed up on a chain's radar.
suggestions.researchNotes: Second Heaton Moor candidate, giving the district its first Do-category venue (previously only Savoy Cinema, already seeded, covered Do). Verified via heatonmoormarket.com, visitmanchester.com and Chamber of Commerce listings: runs 1st Sunday of the month (Feb-Dec), 10.30am-2.30pm, on the Shaw Road car park beside Kro Bar, Heaton Moor SK4 4AG — a real, currently-running civic/community market, not a business itself, so no chain-footprint question applies (same category of entry as Wilmslow Artisan Market/Chorlton Water Park already in venues.json). Type reused (ARTISAN MARKET, Wilmslow Artisan Market precedent). High confidence: actively publicised with dates running through the rest of 2026.

suggestions.name: Cork of the North
suggestions.reason: Five hundred-odd wines by the bottle or the glass and the biggest organic-and-vegan list in the North West, on a Heaton Moor Road unit that opened as the only sibling to a Sale wine shop that came first.
suggestions.researchNotes: Third Heaton Moor candidate today — completes a one-per-category set for the district (Producers Market/Do, Cork of the North/Drink, Avanti/Eat) alongside its 3 existing venues. Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), corkofthenorth.co.uk and manchestersfinest.com: Cork of the North, 104 Heaton Moor Road, Stockport SK4 4NZ, opened 2018, a specialist independent wine shop and wine bar (500+ wines, drink in or take home). Confirmed as a real 2-site pair with the original Sale branch — the same small-sibling-group precedent already accepted for Cibo/Suburban Green/Wallop/Wilmslow's 2-site pairs, well within the line this file has held elsewhere (distinct from the 4-5-site footprints rejected for Reserve Wines, Wood Fire Smoke and Juniper). High confidence: well-documented, independently reviewed, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: By Yon Orange
suggestions.reason: Precision-brewed coffee on Great Underbank in a room design-led enough you'd forgive it for costing more than it does.
suggestions.researchNotes: Stockport (Underbanks) stood at 6 venues (2 Do, 2 Drink, 2 Eat) before this run — bolstering it toward 10 without unbalancing the categories. Verified via Companies House (YON ORANGE LTD, incorporated 25 Feb 2025) and Food Hygiene Ratings: 57 Great Underbank, Stockport SK1 1NE, a minimalist specialty-coffee café, part of the same recent wave of independent openings the Underbanks regeneration has drawn (per Stockport Council's own coverage of the area). No sibling sites or chain footprint found — single, newly incorporated company at one address. Type reused (COFFEE ROOM, Foundation Coffee/Ancoats Coffee Co precedent). Moderate confidence: very recently opened (company incorporated within the last 18 months) so has a thinner review history than most candidates in this batch, but no closure or ownership-ambiguity signals either.

suggestions.name: The Drawing Room
suggestions.reason: Rob and Lorna's forty-five-seat room on Burton Road, life-drawing classes by day and a jukebox nobody's touched in years by night — a Didsbury institution that never needed to get any bigger.
suggestions.researchNotes: Didsbury stood at 8 venues (3 Do, 2 Drink, 3 Eat) before this run — Drink was its thinnest category. Verified via Yelp, DesignMyNight and manchestersfinest.com: The Drawing Room, 148 Burton Road, West Didsbury, Manchester M20 1LH, owned and run by Rob and Lorna (also day-job art lecturers who host life-drawing classes on site) — a long-standing single-site cocktail bar, capacity 45, no sibling locations or chain footprint found. Reserve Wines (176 Burton Road) was also researched for this slot and explicitly rejected: a real 4-site operator (West Didsbury, Altrincham Market, Mackie Mayor, Picturedrome Macclesfield) — the same 4-site line this file has already rejected once for Wood Fire Smoke, so dropped rather than guessed at, even though its Altrincham/Mackie Mayor/Picturedrome concessions sit inside venues already seeded here. High confidence for The Drawing Room: well-established local institution, consistently covered, no closure signals.
